rationale: Luke tells the same two Sabbath scenes in the same order: the grainfields, David and the consecrated bread, "The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath" (Luke 6:5, identical in the BSB to Matthew 12:8), then the man with the withered hand and "Stretch out your hand" (6:10). Parallel/strong rather than explicit, following conn-matt11-woes-luke10, because neither Gospel names the other and the differences can be checked in the BSB. Luke alone says the disciples "rub them in their hands" (6:1), that the healing was "On another Sabbath" (6:6), and that it was the man's "right hand" (6:6). Like Mark, Luke has no priests in the temple, no "something greater than the temple," no Hosea 6:6 and no sheep in the pit; a sheep-like argument appears elsewhere in Luke ("Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day," 14:5). The ending differs most: Matthew 12:14 says the Pharisees "plotted how they might kill Jesus," while Luke 6:11 says "the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus."
